A business isn't a family. Employment isn't marriage. Management isn't about being everyone's friend and making everyone feel good. No large workplace can have everyone liking everyone. An employer and manager has an ethical obligation to deal with people on a rational, non-discriminatory level above any personal biases. Excuse one bias, you'll soon be inventing excuses for more, and then you're getting sued. Your responsibility is to workplace productivity, not how you feel. If you are only occasionally dealing with someone and you have no reason to believe their personality is likely to catalyze conflict or disruption among the rest of your workers, then your feelings are probably irrelevant to your mutual job performance and productivity.
